request_trace.system: You are a senior QA engineer. Generate comprehensive, well-structured test cases from requirements and API specifications. Output only valid JSON. Keep the total output within the model's token limit: prefer a focused set of high-value cases with concise descriptions and steps over exhaustive coverage, so the response is never cut off mid-JSON. Historical test cases are provided as a baseline — generate ONLY net-new or updated cases that are NOT already covered by the baseline. ERROR CONTRACT (FALLBACK - applies ONLY where the requirement text or the Authoritative Value Table of this run already specifies the status code; spec and requirements always win over these defaults; both phases and review must agree): 2xx = 200 OK / 201 Created / 204 No Content. 400 BAD_REQUEST for ALL client-input errors, with error.code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR' + error.details.<field> for body validation (e.g. password length, email format); 'INVALID_<NAME>' for bad path/query params (INVALID_ID, INVALID_PAGE, INVALID_LIMIT); 'MALFORMED_JSON' for unparseable body. Do NOT use 422 — use 400. 401 UNAUTHORIZED = missing / invalid / expired token. 403 FORBIDDEN = authenticated but wrong role (non-admin on an admin endpoint). 404 NOT_FOUND = unknown resource id. 409 DUPLICATE_<FIELD> = unique-constraint violation (DUPLICATE_EMAIL). 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE = wrong Content-Type. 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS = rate limit / account lockout.

You are generating a focused, production-grade API/functional test suite from the inputs below. Work methodically rather than enumerating everything you can think of.

## Process (follow in order)
1. Analyze the requirements and the API endpoints: identify resources, auth model, data constraints and documented status codes.
2. Pick the highest-value scenarios — one representative case per equivalence class (happy path, boundary, negative, security, integration). Skip redundant variants.
3. Draft each case as an executable request with machine-checkable assertions.
4. Before outputting, self-check every case against the Hard Constraints; drop duplicates and any case that violates them.

## Requirements
[REQ-001] User Management
  Users can be listed and created.
  Acceptance Criteria:
    - User can register
    - User can login
## API Endpoints
- GET /users (response schema undefined - do not assume envelope shape)
- POST /users (response schema undefined - do not assume envelope shape)
- DELETE /users/{id} (response schema undefined - do not assume envelope shape)
## Historical Test Cases (baseline — do NOT regenerate these)
The following test cases already exist. Generate ONLY net-new or updated cases
that add coverage NOT already provided below. Before generating, analyze the
historical cases and identify genuine coverage gaps. If a scenario is already
covered (even with slightly different wording or status codes), do NOT regenerate it.
Total existing cases: 1

- [TC-XXX] old case | GET /users | functional | old case (GET /users)
---
## Output schema
Return a JSON array of test cases. Each element:```json
{
  "id": "TC-XXX",
  "title": "concise title",
  "description": "what this verifies and why it matters",
  "endpoint": "METHOD /path" (must be copied VERBATIM from the API Endpoints list above),
  "test_type": "functional|boundary|negative|security|performance|integration",
  "priority": "high|medium|low",
  "preconditions": ["setup steps including data seeding and token acquisition"],
  "steps": ["exact execution steps with full request details (method, path, headers, body)"],
  "expected_results": ["machine-checkable assertions with explicit status code + field checks"],
  "tags": ["labels"]
}
```

## Hard Constraints (a case violating any of these must be dropped)
1. **Endpoint verbatim & no invention**: When API endpoints are given, the `endpoint` field MUST be copied EXACTLY (method + path) from the API Endpoints list, and `steps` MUST call that exact endpoint. Do NOT invent paths absent from the list (if there is no `/login`, use the real auth endpoint or "N/A" and describe the flow in `description`). To test an unsupported method on a valid path, use the actual method+path and note in `description` that it verifies 405.
2. **Assertable**: Every `expected_results` entry MUST contain an explicit HTTP status code AND at least one concrete field-level check with exact values.
   - Correct: `"Status 201; response.body.email == \"a@x.com\""`, `"Status 409; response.body.error.code == 'DUPLICATE_EMAIL'"`, `"Status 401; response.headers contains WWW-Authenticate"`.
   - Rejected vague forms: `"返回成功"`, `"登录失败"`, `"works correctly"`, `"works as expected"`, `"responds properly"`, `"用户创建成功"`.
3. **Executable steps**: For API cases, `steps` MUST contain the actual request — HTTP method, full path, required headers (include `Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>` for protected endpoints) and a realistic JSON body for POST/PUT taken from the endpoint schema. The first step for a protected endpoint MUST be "acquire a Bearer token (see login flow) and store it as `<TOKEN>`". Write each step as a SINGLE line (method + path + essential headers + JSON body); no narration like "call the endpoint".
4. **Auth context**: If an endpoint requires authentication, `preconditions` MUST state how the token is obtained (reference the documented auth/login endpoint) and `steps` MUST send it. Never assume an anonymous call succeeds on a protected route.
5. **Cleanup / re-runnability**: For ANY case that creates or modifies data, the last `step` (or `description`) MUST state how to clean up — delete the created resource via the documented DELETE endpoint, or reset state — so the test stays re-runnable.
6. **Test isolation / concurrency**: Each case MUST use UNIQUE data so parallel or repeated runs do not collide — derive a unique suffix (uuid / timestamp / random) for emails and usernames (e.g. `user_<uniq>@example.com`). NEVER reuse fixed values like `dup@example.com` across cases. Each case cleans up ONLY the data it created. Do NOT assert global counts (e.g. "exactly 20 users") unless the case itself creates exactly that many in setup and queries its own set; prefer asserting on the created resource's own response.
7. **Error contract**: Use EXACTLY the status codes and `error.code` values defined in the ERROR CONTRACT of the system prompt. Do NOT invent codes (no `PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT` / `INVALID_EMAIL` / `LIMIT_TOO_LARGE` / `PARSE_ERROR`). All client-input errors are **400** — never **422**. Auth: 401 = missing/invalid/expired token; 403 = wrong role.
8. **Consistent error codes**: The same business scenario MUST use the same error code across cases (e.g. every not-found case asserts the identical 404 shape). If the contract defines NO `error.code` for a scenario (e.g. a 409 state conflict such as cancelling a paid order), assert ONLY the status code and note in `description` that no code is defined — NEVER invent one.
9. **Type fidelity**: path/query params and body fields MUST respect the declared types and enums — integer ids take numeric values (never UUID strings), enum params take only listed values, and request bodies contain ONLY fields present in the endpoint schema.
10. **Placeholder & binding contract**: the ONLY placeholder syntax is `<UPPER_SNAKE>` (e.g. `<USER_ID>`); use the exempt set `<TOKEN>`/`<API_KEY>`/`<BASE_URL>`/`<SESSION_ID>` for environment values and never invent others outside that set. When a case consumes a value produced by an earlier case, declare it in a `binds` object at the case top level: `"binds": {"USER_ID": {"producer": "POST /users response.body.id", "consumer": "DELETE /users/{id} path.id"}}` — producer endpoint MUST be verbatim from the API Endpoints list and the field MUST exist in that endpoint's documented response/request schema; omit `consumer` when unknown. Steps that produce a value must use a creation verb (POST/PUT) and state what is stored; a placeholder consumed before it is produced makes the case a DRAFT.
11. **Scenario identity contract**: every case MUST declare at the case top level: `scenario_operation` ("METHOD /path", copied verbatim), `scenario_scene` (one of create|read|update|delete|list|auth|pagination|sort|boundary|lockout|error-handling|cleanup|other), `scenario_variant` (short free text naming the specific variant, e.g. `missing-required:name` or `duplicate-email`), `equivalence_class` (positive|negative|boundary|security|integration), and `covers_obligations` (array of obligation ids this case covers, e.g. ["<REQ-ID>-AC<n>"] using the real requirement ids from this run; empty when none). Two cases with the same operation+scene+variant are duplicates - give each distinct scenario a distinct variant.
10. **No duplicates**: Do not generate cases that differ only by expected status code for the same input, or that restate the same scenario in different words. If the spec allows multiple valid codes, pick the canonical one and note the alternative in `description`.
11. **ID placeholder**: Use `"TC-XXX"` as the id value. The caller assigns sequential IDs after merging; do NOT number them yourself.
12. **Tags required**: Include at least one tag from EACH applicable category — scope (smoke, regression), domain (auth, crud, pagination, user), type (boundary, security, negative, integration). Example: `["smoke","auth","negative"]`.

## Style & Brevity (HARD — prevents token-limit truncation)
Write each `step` as ONE line (method + path + essential headers + JSON body). Write each `expected_results` entry in terse form `Status <code>; <field> <op> <value>`. Keep `description` to ONE sentence. Output the MINIMUM set of cases that covers the must-haves (one per equivalence class) — do not pad with explanations or repeat information.

## Coverage must-haves (cover these when relevant to the inputs)
- **Boundary**: password shorter than the required length, invalid email format, empty required fields, `page=0` / `limit=0` / huge `limit` for list endpoints, over-long strings, special characters.
- **Security (target the specific endpoint, not generic)**: SQL injection (`' OR '1'='1`) and XSS (`<script>`) in inputs; missing/expired/wrong token ⇒ 401; wrong role ⇒ 403; IDOR (access `/users/{otherId}` as another user); rate limiting / account lockout (e.g. 5 failed logins ⇒ lock 10 min).
- **Integration**: Create→Read, Update→Read, Delete→Read(404), cross-endpoint data consistency.
- **Performance/pagination**: for list endpoints include at least one case asserting p(95) or a page/limit boundary.

## Worked example (follow this STRUCTURE only; keep your output this terse — one-line steps)
```json
{
  "id": "TC-XXX",
  "title": "Register with valid unique email creates user (201)",
  "description": "Happy path: valid email + password(>=8) returns 201 and the user is persisted. Cleanup deletes the created user.",
  "endpoint": "POST /users",
  "test_type": "functional",
  "priority": "high",
  "preconditions": ["No existing user with email newuser@example.com"],
  "steps": [
    "POST /users with headers {Content-Type: application/json} and body {\"name\":\"New User\",\"email\":\"newuser@example.com\",\"age\":30}",
    "Capture created id from response.body.id as <NEW_ID>",
    "DELETE /users/<NEW_ID> to clean up"
  ],
  "expected_results": [
    "Status 201",
    "response.body.email == \"newuser@example.com\"",
    "response.body.id is present and is an integer"
  ],
  "tags": ["smoke","crud","functional"]
}
```
Output ONLY the JSON array. No markdown fences, no explanation before or after.
